defaults.score_formula: role score = 100 × matched ÷ (checks − checks not counted against the engine − checks without a reference recording − checks needing a value type the engine lacks), with the counts summed over the role's suites, one decimal. overall = Σ weight × role score ÷ Σ weight over the roles that have a score (role scores rounded first). coverage = 100 × (checks − skipped − not counted − needing a missing type) ÷ (checks − needing a missing type).

crash.label: Crash
crash.meaning: The server died or restarted during the check

divergent.label: Different answer
divergent.meaning: Valid protocol, different answer from the reference: the silent kind a client may not notice

hang.label: Hang
hang.meaning: This session waited past the deadline; the server was otherwise alive

harness_error.label: Not counted (our side)
harness_error.meaning: The measurement failed on our side, not the engine's. Also covers a missing answer that only our own probe saw after our client could not talk to the server at all. A bug of ours, fixed before publishing
harness_error.counted: excluded from the score; lowers coverage

not_applicable.label: Not applicable (counted elsewhere)
not_applicable.meaning: Not run because something the check needs is missing and another check already counts that: a value type the engine refused, a TLS session, the mechanism a per-type check repeats for one type (a binary cursor, a COPY format), or, in the access-method table, something the method did not provide (UPDATE, an index type). The gap is counted once, where it is measured; other checks do not count it again.
not_applicable.counted: excluded from the score and from coverage

observed.label: Unmeasured
observed.meaning: No reference recording for this check, so nothing to compare

protocol_violation.label: Protocol violation
protocol_violation.meaning: The server sent something the protocol forbids

skip.label: Skipped
skip.meaning: Not executed: a prerequisite this engine failed, a setup it rejected, or the target was down
skip.counted: denominator (counts against the score); lowers coverage

skip_excluded.label: Skipped (our side)
skip_excluded.meaning: Skipped because of something on our side, a bug of ours fixed before publishing: our deployment did not enforce the password it gave the engine, or the check it depended on (a prerequisite, or the check after which the target was down) failed on our side
skip_excluded.counted: excluded from the score; lowers coverage

unresponsive.label: Unresponsive
unresponsive.meaning: The port accepted TCP but the server stopped answering the protocol

unsupported.label: Refused
unsupported.meaning: Clean, spec-shaped refusal, such as SQLSTATE 0A000 or ER_NOT_SUPPORTED_YET

roles.control: A target built to misbehave, which shows that failures are attributed to the right side
roles.reference: An engine whose recording serves as a baseline. Against its own recording its row is self-consistency; against another version's it is version drift. Not a grade either way
roles.subject: An engine claiming compatibility, measured against a reference

layers.L0: Framing: handshake, auth, session control, message flows
layers.L1: Types: what the wire says a value is and how it is encoded
layers.L2: Introspection: catalog and admin shapes tools rely on
layers.L4: Ecosystem: upstream driver and spec suites

legend.scoring: Every check has one outcome. A role's score is the share of judgeable checks that matched the reference; failed prerequisites count as failures, because a client hits them too. Checks that failed on our side and checks with no reference recording are left out; a row where nothing is left has no score and says why in its note. The overall score weighs frames 0.35, types 0.25, bulk 0.25, upstream 0.15, renormalized over the roles that have a score. Raw counts are published so any other weighting can be computed. role score = 100 × matched ÷ (checks − checks not counted against the engine − checks without a reference recording − checks needing a value type the engine lacks), with the counts summed over the role's suites, one decimal. overall = Σ weight × role score ÷ Σ weight over the roles that have a score (role scores rounded first). coverage = 100 × (checks − skipped − not counted − needing a missing type) ÷ (checks − needing a missing type).
legend.baselines: Each engine is compared with a reference engine of the same protocol: the reference for the version it claims when one is recorded (PostgreSQL 13–18, MySQL 8.0/8.4/9), otherwise the protocol default. The row states which reference and why. Differences are counted as differences even when an engine documents them as intentional.
caveats: Tier 0 is the wire contract only: frames, types and bulk load. It is not the SQL dialect, performance, durability or feature coverage. A high score means drivers and tools can talk to the engine as they do to the reference; it does not mean your queries behave the same.

Checks talk to an engine the way the protocol's own clients do, SQL included: for PostgreSQL wire, the way PostgreSQL's test suites and pgx do, with :: casts, pg_sleep, generate_series and other PostgreSQL SQL. An engine that speaks the wire format with a different SQL dialect is measured as it answers that SQL; the finding names the construct.
Scores are relative to a reference engine, not to a specification; a reference's own quirks are expected behavior here.
Results caused by our side never count against an engine. They are listed in each row's details, and a dataset that has any is not published.

A reference compared with its own recording should score 100; anything less is measurement noise we have to fix, and it bounds how precise the other rows are. References compared with another version show drift between versions of the same engine.
Each row is one run of one image (digest given) at one time. Other versions and configurations may differ.
The weights are a default, not a verdict. Every count is published so the scores can be recomputed.
Plain-words summaries are generated mechanically from the first difference of each root cause; the check ids and the observed-vs-expected example are the evidence.
Reproduce a row: conformity run -t <target> --protocol <protocol> --baseline <reference>, or one check with --check <check id>, using the tool version and image digest the details give.

Contest a finding by opening an issue at github.com/stroppy-io/stroppy-conformity with the check id and run id. Findings are evidence, not opinion: the run id names the full report, frame traces included, and a confirmed harness bug is fixed and the row re-measured.

The access-method table compares a table access method with heap in the same server image and version, so changes the image makes to the server itself are not counted against the method. Rows of a statement without ORDER BY compare as a multiset there, since a method may return them in its own order. Its overall score weighs upstream 0.15, access_method 0.85.

feature_codes.label: Match
feature_codes.meaning: every judged check matched the reference

feature_codes.label: Not judged
feature_codes.meaning: checks ran but none could be judged: no reference recording, or blamed on the measuring side

feature_codes.label: Skipped
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a skip: a prerequisite failed

feature_codes.label: Refused
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a clean, spec-shaped refusal

feature_codes.label: Different answer
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a valid answer that differs from the reference

feature_codes.label: Protocol violation
feature_codes.meaning: worst is something the protocol forbids

feature_codes.label: Hang
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a session left without an answer

feature_codes.label: Unresponsive
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a server that stopped answering

feature_codes.label: Crash
feature_codes.meaning: worst is a server that died or restarted

legend.feature_cells: feature_cells[k] describes features[feature_sets[protocol][k]] for a row of that protocol: null when the row has no check of that feature, otherwise [code, matched, total]. code is the worst outcome (legend.feature_codes; higher is worse), matched the checks that matched, total the checks that count toward a score (the role score's denominator).
legend.supported_types_filter: Filter out unsupported types: re-scores every row without the checks that need a value type the engine does not support, meaning its type check was refused, or could not run because a type it needs is missing. A type the engine supports but encodes differently from the reference is kept, and its differences still count. Off by default; the numbers it shows are published beside the default ones as scores_supported_types and counts_supported_types.
